items.stem: In a series hybrid operating in normal mode, how does power normally reach the driven wheels?

options.text: Directly from the internal combustion engine through a gearbox
options.rationale: In a pure series hybrid the engine has no mechanical path to the wheels.

options.text: From an electric motor, with the engine driving a generator
options.rationale: In series mode the engine drives a generator and the electric motor alone propels the wheels.

options.text: Only from the battery, with the engine never running
options.rationale: The engine runs to generate electricity when needed.

options.text: From a belt connecting the engine crankshaft to the axle
options.rationale: No such direct belt drive to the axle exists in a series hybrid.

items.explanation: In series mode the engine drives a generator and the electric motor alone propels the wheels.

items.stem: Which statement best describes a mild hybrid compared with a full hybrid?

options.text: A mild hybrid can drive on electric power alone for extended distances
options.rationale: That capability characterises full and plug-in hybrids, not mild hybrids.

options.text: A mild hybrid assists the engine and enables start-stop but cannot drive on electric power alone
options.rationale: Mild hybrids provide torque assist and smoother start-stop but have no sustained electric-only propulsion.

options.text: A mild hybrid has a larger battery than a plug-in hybrid
options.rationale: Plug-in hybrids have substantially larger batteries.

options.text: A mild hybrid has no electric machine at all
options.rationale: A mild hybrid includes a small electric machine for assist and start-stop.

items.explanation: Mild hybrids provide torque assist and smoother start-stop but have no sustained electric-only propulsion.

items.stem: A hybrid controller decides when to recover energy. Select TWO conditions under which regenerative braking is most effective at recovering energy.

options.text: During frequent decelerations in city driving
options.rationale: Repeated braking events in city driving offer many opportunities to recover kinetic energy.

options.text: When the battery has headroom to accept charge
options.rationale: Energy can only be stored if the battery is not already near full state of charge.

options.text: When the battery is already fully charged
options.rationale: A full battery cannot accept regenerated energy, so recovery is limited.
Steady cruising involves little braking, so there is little energy to recover.

options.text: When the vehicle is parked and switched off
options.rationale: No kinetic energy is available to recover when stationary.

items.explanation: Repeated braking events in city driving offer many opportunities to recover kinetic energy.
